claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do! I have one child, Alex, who's 18 and still lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand a bit more about their situation.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. A-level study at sixth form college typically counts as approved education.

Can you tell me when Alex turned 18, or what date their 18th birthday was?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 18 in September, so just a few months ago.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. One more important question: when does Alex's current course of education end, or when is he expected to finish his A-levels?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's expected to finish his A-levels in June next year, so he's got about another 8 or 9 months left of his course.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why: Even though Alex is 18, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for young people aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training. A-level study at sixth form college qualifies as approved education.

Since Alex:
- Is 18 years old (under 20)
- Is currently studying for his A-levels at sixth form college
- Will finish his course in June next year

You will remain eligible for Child Benefit for Alex until **31st August next year** (the 31st August following the completion of his A-level course).

After that date, once his approved education ends, your entitlement to Child Benefit for Alex will stop.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your Child Benefit entitlement?

reasonings: Alex turned 18 in September and is currently studying for his A-levels at sixth form college, with the course ending in June next year. Under UK Child Benefit rules, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for a young person aged 16-19 if they are in approved education or training. A-level study at sixth form college qualifies as approved education. Child Benefit continues until the young person turns 20, or until they finish their approved education or training (whichever comes first). The benefit stops on the 31st August following the completion of the course, or when they turn 20. Since Alex is 18, still in approved full-time education (A-levels), and will finish his course in June (before turning 20), you remain eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. The benefit would continue until 31st August next year, after his course completes.
